dinkum-4.meaning: Both notices kept whole: "From Friday, Sept. 4, the last of the fishing restrictions", "Part-day restrictions still on from 2 p.m. till sunrise the next day", "plus rain in the current forecast", and every handling instruction ("Don't play hooked trout till they're knackered").
dinkum-4.sense: Terms fit: "all the creeks that feed 'em" for tributaries, "wet a line", "quick smart", "till they're knackered", "let 'em get their breath back". "once things picked up" for "as conditions improved" is right.
dinkum-4.authenticity: Natural angler talk: "wet a line", "land fish quick smart", "Pitchin' in like this". The clipped endings are applied evenly rather than overdone.
dinkum-4.register: About level 3 to 4: steady slang and clipped speech ("cos", "Park staff'll", "dependin'"), but the notice structure and much plain wording stay ("Temporary restrictions could be lifted, or more closures put in"). Short of a full level-5 yarn. No swearing, within the dial.
dinkum-4.tone: Keeps the notice's informative tone and its earnest closing plea: "Please fish in the coolest part of the day".
dinkum-4.flow: Reads smoothly: "The water's been coolin' off overnight, so there's fishin' for part of the day."
dinkum-4.variety: Good spread ("wet a line", "quick smart", "knackered", "get their breath back", "Pitchin' in"), with the repeated notice lines ("Park staff'll keep an eye on the water temperatures") echoing the original's own repetition.
dinkum-4.essence: Unmistakably the two-part park notice, retold.

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Everything kept: "from sunup till 2 p.m. each day", "a bit of rain in the current forecast", "it might save the park havin' to ban fishin' at all hours".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Mostly exact: "till they're stuffed", "let 'em come good", "Anglers'll be right to fish". "which can knock fish off" for lethal is a jokey kill sense that sits oddly in a conservation warning.
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural: "Anglers'll be right to fish these rivers", "how they rate the conditions", "let 'em come good". Mixes "fishin'" with an unclipped "Depending".
yarn-dinkum.register: About level 3 to 4: clipped speech and slang ("sunup to sundown", "stuffed", "come good", "cos"), but keeps the notice shape and much notice wording ("every tributary that runs into 'em"). Short of a full yarn. No swearing.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Mostly keeps the notice's earnest tone; "which can knock fish off" makes the lethal-temperature warning a touch flippant.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth: "With cooler weather and cooler water temperatures, and a bit of rain in the current forecast, the full closures can come off."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "sunup", "knock fish off", "stuffed", "come good", "quick smart", "Pitchin' in". "sunup" recurs often, as the original repeats sunrise.

dinkum-3.meaning: Everything kept, with colour hanging off the original: "Good news for fishos", "If everyone does the right thing, it'll look after the park's fisheries".
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "fishos", "have a go at the Firehole", "Do us a favour", "till it's knackered", "give 'em a chance to come good".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Most like a local talking: "Good news for fishos", "Do us a favour and fish in the coolest part of the day", "If everyone does the right thing". "keep an eye on the water temperatures, mind" uses a British tag.
dinkum-3.register: Nearest to level 5: addresses the reader as a mate ("You'll be able to fish", "Ya can still fish"), adds a spoken opener and "Do us a favour". Still keeps the notice skeleton and headers. No swearing, within the dial.
dinkum-3.tone: Keeps the notice and the plea; "Do us a favour" stays polite and the warnings stay serious ("which can kill fish").
dinkum-3.flow: Mostly smooth, but "The full closures went on back on July 15" stumbles.
dinkum-3.variety: The widest spread: "fishos", "have a go", "Do us a favour", "knackered", "come good", "does the right thing", "mind". "Depending on how things are lookin'" appears twice.
dinkum-3.essence: Unmistakably the two-part park notice, now spoken to fishos.

dinkum-4.quote: Temporary restrictions could be lifted, or more closures put in, dependin' on how conditions look.
dinkum-4.original: Temporary restrictions may be lifted, or additional closures may be put in place, depending on condition assessments.
dinkum-4.why: Stays close to notice English, light for a level-5 brief.

yarn-dinkum.original: that can be lethal to fish
yarn-dinkum.why: Knock off as kill is jokey; lightens a serious warning.

dinkum-3.quote: Staff'll keep an eye on the water temperatures, mind.
dinkum-3.original: Staff will continue to monitor the water temperatures.
dinkum-3.why: The mind tag is British or Northern English, not Australian.

dinkum-3.quote: The full closures went on back on July 15
dinkum-3.original: The full closures were implemented on July 15
dinkum-3.why: Went on back on is a clunky join.

summaries.dinkum-4: Accurate, natural and smooth, but lighter than the full level 5 asked.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Accurate and natural, a touch flippant on the lethal-temperature line, and lighter than level 5.
summaries.dinkum-3: The most Aussie and the most reader-facing, closest to the level 5 asked, with a couple of slips.
